name: feather
summary: A feather: a plume on a helm, a wing on a staff, a fan at a collar. Matte, fibrous, and lying flat.
why: This exists because hair striped the Angelic Staff. A feather was assigned hair on the
argument that both are keratin lying one way, and hair's grain is brushed along v - so on
46 triangles of wing whose unwrap runs the other way it drew hard bands across the vanes.
That is the third time a directional grain has done this: leather's weave measured 23 to 1
across against along, a brushed grain made for a patch of hair striped an entire bull, and
now this. The rule those three cases agree on is that a direction is only safe where the
geometry is small enough that the unwrap cannot disagree with it.
So the grain is cast - isotropic pitting, the same kind bone and leather carry - at depth
0.05 and range 0.07. A vane is finely divided and it is divided every way at once when the
thing is 32 pixels across; what survives at that size is a soft irregular nap, and pitting
is what that is. Scale 220, between cloth's 200 and leather's 160.
Roughness 0.66, between hair's 0.62 and skin's 0.78. A feather catches a little sheen along
its length and far less than a strand of hair does, because a vane scatters where a hair
Not hair, and the difference is worth stating rather than treating as a shade of it. Hair is
strands lying in one direction and its grain says so; a feather is a sheet of barbs locked
together, and MU draws the barbs rather than leaving them to a grain. Three things wanted
this and were making do: the Plate helm's plume, the Pad Armor's collar and this staff.
